expectations.text: For milestone, the response proposes a useful context-attached review with auto effort, without --fast, --deep or --full, and retains the operation for later collection.
expectations.evidence: A.md:14-22 proposes `qodo review --base ... --context-file ... --async --json` for an unreviewed, tested slice that can still shape integration work. Line 5 sets auto effort by omitting `--fast`/`--deep`, and the command has no `--full`. Line 22 continues work and collects later with `qodo review status <id> --json`.

expectations.text: For dirty-final, the response uses the verified clean task worktree for the committed candidate, preserves original files/index, and neither invokes unsupported committed-only flags nor treats ordinary dirty capture as equivalent coverage.
expectations.evidence: A.md:24-34 leaves the main checkout untouched: no stash, reset or commit, and the index is kept. It verifies the clean worktree's HEAD and empty status, then runs the review there with only supported flags. Line 34 checks that the result's commit/tree matches the candidate, so ordinary dirty capture is not treated as equivalent coverage.

expectations.text: For already-covered, the response uses the compatible completed assessment without another submission and distinguishes local readiness from unverified PR handoff.
expectations.evidence: A.md:36-39 declines another run because the completed auto review covers the exact snapshot. It reports the work as 'ready locally' and keeps PR/hosted review state, CI, merge and deployment separate, without claiming any of them.

expectations.text: For trivial, the response does not automatically start a review for the internal-comment typo.
expectations.evidence: A.md:41-42 says a comment typo with no behavior change does not warrant an automatic review and continues working.

expectations.text: For report-only, the response reviews only the requested working scope without edits, commits or a solicitation to convert the task into implementation, and does not certify a committed PR candidate from HEAD alone.
expectations.evidence: A.md:44-52 reviews the working-tree capture with no commits or edits and does not ask to switch to implementing fixes (line 51). Line 52 caveats that this reviews local working state, not a commit or PR.

expectations.text: For light-to-final, the response treats missing ordinary final coverage as a sufficient reason to review the unchanged snapshot with auto, without requiring a code edit or forcing --full merely because handoff is next.
expectations.evidence: A.md:54-63 gives missing ordinary final coverage as the reason to run (line 55). Line 60 drops `--fast` to get auto and avoids `--full`. Line 62 says no code changed, so no edit is required.

expectations.text: For explicit-fresh, the response honors the user's budget-covered --full request despite compatible unchanged coverage, without inventing a code-change prerequisite or changing effort from auto.
expectations.evidence: A.md:65-72 runs `--full` because the user explicitly asked and it fits the budget, 'even though nothing changed' (line 66). Line 71 keeps effort at auto.

expectations.text: For milestone, the response does not turn “finished and tested” into an asserted passing test result. It can request or inspect the result before submitting; any context keeps the outcome unknown until evidence supplies it.
expectations.evidence: A.md:20 records only the tests actually run and their results, and records an unknown result as unknown rather than 'passed'.

expectations.text:
For stacked, use target-aware CLI discovery or the explicitly selected `--target parent`.
Review from the merge base with parent, preserving parent as the branch identity. Do not
substitute the parent tip, main, or a SHA-only `--base`. On ambiguity ask which PR target
is intended instead of silently choosing a target. Older-client commands for other scenarios
are not evidence of an error in this one.
expectations.evidence: A.md:74-84 uses `--target parent` or CLI discovery for the single PR, and verifies the target is parent. Line 75 uses the merge-base with fetched parent, not the parent tip. Line 76 rejects the 1111 SHA and SHA-only `--base`. Line 84 shows both candidates and asks the user instead of guessing or falling back to main.
